exercise.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row

reference.title: Dumbbell Bent Over Row
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Back, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder extension, scapular retraction, elbow flexion; isometric hip hinge)

breathing.pattern: Brace, exhale as you row, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; stop about 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3)
prescription.progression: Add load or reps; pause at the top

cues.text: Feet hip width, soft knees, hinge at the hips with a flat back (trunk about 35-45 degrees above the floor), dumbbells hanging under the shoulders.
Breathe out and drive the elbow up and back toward the hip, close to the body.
Squeeze the shoulder blade back; the dumbbell reaches the side of the lower ribs.
Breathe in and lower under control until the arm is straight.
Let the shoulder blade glide forward a little, keep the back flat, repeat.

mistakes.fix: Push the hips back, keep the chest proud and the spine long; hinge less if needed.
Keep the trunk angle fixed; use lighter dumbbells.
Drive the elbows back toward the hips.

kinematics.norm: About 30-45 degrees above the floor with a neutral spine (clinical opinion); the standing bent-over row produced the most lumbar flexion of the rows in Fenwick 2009, so keep it neutral
From nearly straight to about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #029312, Dumbbell Bent Over Row, video (movement reference)
Fenwick, Brown & McGill 2009, comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load and stiffness (J Strength Cond Res 23(2):350-358)
Edelburg 2017, electromyographic analysis of the back muscles during various back exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
The dumbbell load is your choice: pick a weight you can move with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low-back pain: this row loads the low back more than supported rows (Fenwick 2009); choose the chest-supported or one-arm bench row instead.
modify: Tight hamstrings: bend the knees more and hinge a little less.
Shoulder pain: shorten the top of the range.
regressions: One-arm dumbbell row on a bench.
progressions: Lower trunk angle (closer to parallel) if the back stays flat.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Extend the shoulders, pulling the elbows back past the trunk. Barbell bent-over rows reached about 91% MVC in the latissimus in Edelburg 2017.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Extend the shoulders, pulling the elbows back past the trunk. Barbell bent-over rows reached about 91% MVC in the latissimus in Edelburg 2017.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Retract the shoulder blades at the top; the bent-over row was among the highest middle trapezius activities in Edelburg 2017 (about 107% MVC).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Retract the shoulder blades at the top; the bent-over row was among the highest middle trapezius activities in Edelburg 2017 (about 107% MVC).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Flex the elbows to about 90 degrees.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Flex the elbows to about 90 degrees.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the hinged trunk still. Lumbar erector activity (about 43% MVC) and lumbar compression (about 3.6 kN) were highest in the standing bent-over row of the rows compared by Fenwick 2009; Edelburg 2017 also found the highest erector activity in the bent-over row.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the hinged trunk still. Lumbar erector activity (about 43% MVC) and lumbar compression (about 3.6 kN) were highest in the standing bent-over row of the rows compared by Fenwick 2009; Edelburg 2017 also found the highest erector activity in the bent-over row.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Holds the hip hinge with the hamstrings.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Holds the hip hinge with the hamstrings.
muscleNotes.core: Brace the trunk so the spine stays neutral.
